title: improv·artist · fluid (Helen Frankenthaler)
mutation_directive: improv artist: fluid via Helen Frankenthaler

improv_extras.practice: soak-stain; thinned pigment soaks the canvas; geological flow

v1.feedback: The three stain pools are radially symmetric circles — Frankenthaler's soak-stain edges are defined by capillary irregularity, not uniform radial falloff. Replace the uniform radial init with a noise-warped boundary (e.g. FBM displacement on the radius) so each pool has an organic, meandering silhouette. The 0.98 per-frame damping kills all motion in ~2s, turning 'geological flow' into a frozen snapshot; use a persistent low-magnitude flow field (curl of a 2D potential) so pigment keeps creeping slowly outward with visible front edges. Where two stain pools overlap there is no color interaction — add subtractive or min-blend mixing in the overlap region to simulate wet-on-wet bleeding, which is the signature Frankenthaler effect this piece is missing.

v2.feedback: The three-pool layout with subtractive overlap mixing and warm-paper background correctly references Frankenthaler, but the pools read as noisy circles rather than soak-stains — real stain edges feather with directional tendrils and concentration gradients, not uniform FBM displacement. Add per-particle opacity falloff tied to distance from pool center (denser pigment near origin, transparent bleed at edges) and replace the isotropic curl field with a gravity-biased downward flow so pigment visibly 'soaks' in one direction, giving the geological-flow quality the brief asks for. The color mixing recompute loop (70k × 3 pools every 0.5s) is fine now but will stall on low-end GPUs — consider spatial hashing or just baking the mix at spawn and letting flow handle the rest.
